analysis.title: GS Garrett - weekend prep 18 Oct 2026
key_insights: Momentum and the AI complex are under pressure and AI capex and funding concerns are back in focus, heading into the heart of US earnings season. Garrett argues the next move depends more on earnings confirmation than anything else. 14% of SPX reports the coming week and 44% the week after.

Positioning is very low. Net exposure in the US long/short cohort is at the lowest level in 5 years. GS Prime data shows tech had its largest ever 1-week net selling in dataset history, with net exposure and L/S ratio both at the 0th percentile.

Garrett reads the index sell-off as a 'close the gap' / 'misery loves company' move rather than a material portfolio risk adjustment. Fear of benchmark underperformance remains, after SPX hit an all-time high last week.

Breadth is improving ('the revenge of everything else'). The market had been narrow, with 10 names making up almost 40% of the index. 350 SPX companies were green last week and SPX ex-AI outperformed SPX by 475bps.
The outperformance option pitched last week (SPX ex-AI vs SPX) is already at breakeven with 3 months to go.

The debt burden across AI is described as not new news. The 'AI borrowing flooding debt markets' framing comes from a WSJ article a year old, and the current environment should not be confused with an unknown unknown. Garrett still acknowledges the size and scope of the issuance.
Credit is flashing stress. CCCs broke above 1000bps spread to benchmark relative to the rest of HY, and CDX IG is 'flinching' significantly more than the 1-month VIX future.

Fundamental long/short managers lost 2.7% on the week (alpha -1.1%) and 2.8% on the month (alpha -1.6%), and are up 9.8% on the year on a weighted average, a figure Garrett says feels high relative to floor conversations.

US central long/short hedge fund net exposure fell by the largest weekly decline since liberation day (-3.2) and sits at the 0th percentile on 1y, 2y and 5y horizons. TMT was the most net-sold in the dataset's history.
Gross exposure did not fall with net. It remains at 213.9% (83rd percentile, 3y), so funds have gotten less long but not smaller.

Asset managers were better sellers, with sell skews in tech and macro product against demand in financials. Hedge funds were net sellers of both macro (ETFs) and tech, so both cohorts were selling megacaps.
Semiconductors were down 8 sessions in a row, the longest streak since 2006, and are near oversold on RSI for only the second time in 4 years.

CTA questions have moved from equities to government bonds. With TLT up 7 sessions in a row, GS expects CTAs to be short about $164mm/bp DV01 globally, with a baseline forecast to buy $12mm DV01 over 1 week and $65mm DV01 over 1 month.
Friday was the largest SPX put volume session of all time, with over $3.3 trillion notional traded.

The 'GS panic' index started the week at a one handle and finished at 7.4, one of the sharpest rallies on record. The 'delta adjusted VIX' showed one of the largest sessions of VIX outperformance in 3 years.
Pre-market single stock options begin trading on 29 tickers on Monday, with the first session 7:30a-9:25a.
The 'AI winners' vs 'AI at risk' basket pair trade is flat on the year, after being up almost 100% from 1 Jan 2026 through end of June.
